paper_metadata.title: Influence of Ru on high-temperature creep rupture properties and oxidation behavior of Ni-based single-crystal superalloys

evidence.quote: The present study investigates the microstructure, high-temperature creep rupture properties and oxidation resistance of three fourth-generation single-crystal Ni-based superalloys containing 0, 3.5 and 7 wt% of Ru.

As Ru content rises, the γ’-forming elements such as Al and Ta exhibit increasing partitioning preference into γ, and conversely, all γ-forming elements showed higher partitioning preference into γ’.

Previous investigations show that the high-temperature performance of superalloys would be significantly improved by Re addition due to solid-solution strengthening and a more negative γ/γ’ lattice misfit [3–5].
The generation of large amount of creep cavities in alloy 7Ru under 1150 °C may be associated with enhanced dislocation climbing.
The thermal stress and possible Re evaporation generated voids and cracks in the vicinity of the unoxidized Ru particles, which facilitated oxygen diffusion.

The precipitation of TCP phase is suppressed as Ru content increases, which can be attributed to the so-called “partitioning reversal” phenomenon [41], that is, the addition of Ru causes more γ formers to be partitioned into γ’.
